vulnerabilities.description: Session files and helper scripts are world-readable (rw-rw-r--). Session data could be read by other users on shared systems. Session IDs are predictable using only Date.now().
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Change file permissions to 600 (rw-------), use cryptographically secure random session ID generation

vulnerabilities.description: Memory storage files are world-readable (rw-rw-r--). Sensitive data stored in JSON could be exposed to other users.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Change file permissions to 600, implement encryption for stored data, validate data before parsing

vulnerabilities.description: Data directory and all JSON files are world-readable and world-writable (rw-rw-r--). Stored data includes application state and metrics.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Change directory and file permissions to 700 (rwx------) and 600 (rw------) respectively

vulnerabilities.description: Session IDs generated using only timestamp: session-${Date.now()}. Timestamps are sequential and predictable.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Use randomBytes or crypto.randomUUID() for session ID generation

vulnerabilities.description: Session and memory data stored in plain text JSON files without encryption.
vulnerabilities.impact: Sensitive data exposure if filesystem is compromised
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Implement encryption using Node.js crypto module for sensitive data

passed_checks.detail: No hardcoded API keys, passwords, or credentials found in source code. NEXT_PUBLIC_* variables properly used for public config.
No SQL queries found. This is a static site generator (SSG) with no backend database. No database-related vulnerabilities.
Only safe dangerouslySetInnerHTML usage found (hardcoded theme script). All user input properly escaped in React components.
No eval(), Function constructor, or dynamic code execution found. Subprocess spawning uses spawnSync without shell interpretation.
Modern, up-to-date dependencies: Next.js 14.2.35, React 18, Tailwind CSS 3.4.19. No known vulnerable packages detected.
memory.js validates keys with /^[a-z0-9_]+$/i. localStorage data has try-catch error handling.
Static site (SSG output). Cross-origin requests only to Google APIs (fonts, analytics, ads) with proper crossOrigin attributes.
No authentication required. Public calculator site. No sensitive auth mechanisms exposed.

recommendations.title: Fix File Permissions
recommendations.description: Change helper scripts and data directories to restrict access to the owner only

recommendations.title: Secure Session ID Generation
recommendations.description: Replace predictable session IDs with cryptographically secure random values
steps: Add uuid or nanoid library if needed
Test session ID uniqueness and unpredictability

recommendations.title: Encrypt Stored Data
recommendations.description: Implement encryption for session and memory data files
steps: Use Node.js crypto module with AES-256-GCM
Derive encryption key from a master secret or key file
Add encryption/decryption to memory.js and session.js

recommendations.title: Add Security Documentation
recommendations.description: Create SECURITY.md file documenting security practices and permissions

recommendations.title: Add Session Expiration
recommendations.description: Implement session timeout and cleanup mechanism
steps: Implement periodic cleanup of expired sessions

summary.key_findings: Codebase is generally secure with no critical vulnerabilities. Main concerns are file system permissions on helper scripts and data directories (world-readable), and predictable session ID generation. The application properly handles input validation, avoids injection attacks, and maintains up-to-date dependencies.
